snippet.title: The Real Boardwalk Empire: How the Mafia Secretly Took Over Atlantic City
snippet.description:
In November of 1928, Arnold Rothstein bled out in a Manhattan hotel room and refused to name his killer. Seven months later, the most dangerous men in America gathered on the Atlantic City boardwalk to divide up the country. 

This is the real story behind HBO’s Boardwalk Empire, and it’s bloodier, richer, and stranger than the show ever dared to be.

Step inside the true history of Enoch “Nucky” Johnson, the 6 foot 4 political boss who ran Atlantic City like his personal kingdom for 30 years, earning an estimated $500,000 a year tax free at the height of Prohibition. Watch how Al Capone built a $100 million a year empire in Chicago, only to be destroyed by an accountant tracing unpaid taxes. Discover how Charlie “Lucky” Luciano restructured American organized crime forever after eliminating his two bosses in 1931, then cut a wartime deal with the U.S. Navy that walked him out of a 30 to 50 year sentence. And learn why Meyer Lansky, the quiet financial genius, was the only one who truly won.

In this documentary you will learn:
- The real events of the 1929 Atlantic City Conference and the 3 decisions that built the modern Mafia
- How Nucky Johnson controlled politicians, police, and the press for 3 decades
- The exact tax evasion case that took down Al Capone in 1931
- The shocking deal called Operation Underworld that freed Luciano during World War 2
- Why Meyer Lansky beat every charge and died wealthy in his own bed
- What HBO got right, and the brutal truths they had to leave out

Key figures covered: 
Nucky Johnson, Al Capone, Charlie “Lucky” Luciano, Meyer Lansky, Arnold Rothstein, Bugsy Siegel, Frank Costello, Thomas Dewey, Joe Masseria, and Salvatore Maranzano. Timeline: 1919 to 1983.

This story matters because the rules these men wrote on a boardwalk in May 1929 still define organized crime today. From cartel finance to political corruption, the playbook they invented is still being used.

snippet.description:
How did Britain stop Hitler’s seemingly unstoppable air force in 1940? 🔔 Subscribe and join us on this journey around the world → https://bit.ly/WorldView-Documentary

A story of human endeavour, the contest between British and German airforces in 1940 which became a defining point of the Second World War. With unseen footage from the feature film, Battle of Britain, this series provides an unbiased accounts of the events in the skies above Britain. A chronological account of a country preparing to defend itself against a rising empire.

Part 1 – The Few
By May 1940, the die was cast and the war started in earnest. This episode examines the build-up to the Battle of Britain, studying the technological advances that the RAF pioneered, to the start of the Battle itself.  At the heart of the RAF production were two world-class fighters – theHurricane & the Spitfire, able to compete against the best that the Luftwaffe had to offer.

Part 2 – Darkest Hour
This focuses on events from July to early Sept. 1940, where both sides were finding their feet.  The Germans tried initially to bomb British naval shipping with limited success. Three separate attacks in August, targeting RAF airfields were successful – Biggin Hill, North Weald & Kenley were all put out of action – albeit temporarily. Then the Germans made a mistake that ultimately lost them the war.

Part 3 – The Blitz
During the first week of September, Hitler decided to move the bombing strategy away from the airfields, to civilian London. This episode examines the spirit of the Londoners who defied Hitler, and ultimately ended the war in the last weeks of September. The RAF with fewer resources, fewer men & machines had beaten the might of the Luftwaffe.

snippet.title: Chicago Buildings Are Killing Birds. ‘Flyway City’ Exhibit Is Architect Jeanne Gang’s Call To Action
snippet.description:
Chicago’s Jeanne Gang is arguably one of the best-known architects working today. She’s spending whatever social capital comes with that reputation to argue for better building design — not just for humans but for wildlife, particularly birds.
 
A passionate birder herself, Gang has made bird-friendly design central to her practice, from the highly lauded Aqua Tower that soars above Lakeshore East to her company’s studio in the West Town neighborhood.
 
It’s past time for others to do the same, she said, and that includes Chicago officials who have yet to pass a bird-friendly building design ordinance.
 
“I see this as a sustainability issue. Loss of biodiversity is one of the most important parts of what’s happening with climate change, and we really don’t need to be killing birds with our buildings. It’s not necessary and it’s so avoidable,” Gang said at a preview of the new exhibit, “Flyway City,” now open at the Chicago Architecture Center (@chiarchitecture) and co-curated by her firm, @studiogang.
 
The exhibit grew out of conversations between Gang and Eleanor Gorski, CEO and president of the Chicago Architecture Center, regarding the intersection of the built environment and the natural environment.
 
“We were talking about wildlife, cities, buildings and how the design of both need to respond more fully to wildlife and welcoming wildlife into cities,” Gorski said.
 
“Flyway City” feels very much like a continuation of those discussions, examining the city’s relationship with its winged residents, warts and all.

snippet.title: The Real Boston George Was Far More Dangerous Than The Movie
snippet.description:
George Jacob Jung partied with Pablo Escobar. He cleared $100,000 a day. He helped a single Colombian organization flood America with 85% of its cocaine — and then he died broke in a hospice bed in the same Boston suburb where it all began. This is the real story behind the movie “Blow,” and almost none of it looks like Hollywood told you.

In this deep-dive documentary, we break down the full life of George Jacob Jung, aka “Boston George,” aka “El Americano” — from his working-class childhood in Weymouth, Massachusetts, to a fateful prison cell in Danbury, Connecticut in 1974 where he met a young Colombian-German named Carlos Lehder. Together, they sketched the blueprint for what would become the most efficient cocaine pipeline in American history, running tons of product through Norman’s Cay, a private island in the Bahamas, and into Florida and Georgia.

What you’ll learn in this video:
• How a marijuana smuggler from Manhattan Beach became Pablo Escobar’s American partner
 • The truth about the 1974 Danbury prison cell that changed the global drug trade
 • How Norman’s Cay actually worked as a Bahamas transshipment hub
 • What “Blow” got right and the major characters the film invented or combined
 • The real story of Mirtha Jung, their 1984 divorce, and her road to sobriety
 • Why Kristina Sunshine Jung refused to see her father for decades
 • How George testified against Carlos Lehder in 1987 — and the price he paid
 • The 1994 Topeka, Kansas bust with 1,754 pounds of cocaine and the 60-year sentence
 • What happened to Lehder, Escobar, Mirtha, and Kristina after the empire collapsed
 • Why George died in 2021 with nothing but a memoir, a movie, and a daughter he barely knew

Key figures: 
George Jung, Carlos Lehder, Pablo Escobar, Mirtha Calderon Jung, Kristina Sunshine Jung, the Medellín Cartel.

Timeline: 
1942 (birth) → 1968 (marijuana smuggling begins) → 1974 (Danbury prison) → 1976-1984 (cocaine empire peak) → 1987 (testifies vs. Lehder) → 1994 (final arrest) → 2014 (released) → 2021 (death).

Garcia’s close relationship with the Gambino captain Greg DePalma and key events such as a violent assault in a Bloomingdale's led to the indictment of 32 mobsters. He recounts being proposed for membership in the family before the FBI prematurely ended the investigation. He contrasts the romanticized Italian mob with the greater brutality of drug cartels and discusses other major cases he worked, including police corruption in Hollywood, Florida, and Boston.

Since retiring from the FBI in 2006, Jack has written a New York Times bestseller, "Making Jack Falcone: An Undercover FBI Agent Takes Down a Mafia Family."

Brazil is said to be a sleeping giant waking up to become one of the world leaders. Our film will tell the country’s history through the eyes of two families over several generations.

In one of the families, the slaves of before became domestic workers, and the former domestics are now employees, with fixed hours and living in their own homes, where they raise their own children rather than those of their bosses. They have reached the middle class. The other family descends from coffee barons and army generals. It is still a wealthy family, but yesterday’s fortune was lost. Its members have witnessed many historical events. These two families will embody the evolutions of Brazil since the twenties until today. Our goal is to intersect the families saga and the nation’s history with a broad range of photo and film archives, both public and private. We will complete this with a more global contextualization of the general History of the country.

snippet.title: The Fall of Berlin - How World War II Ended in Brutal Street Battles
snippet.description:
The fall of Berlin marked the end of Nazi Germany - but at what cost? Witness the brutal final days of World War II as the Soviets and Allies closed in on Hitler’s regime.

This gripping video takes you through the collapse of the Third Reich, starting from the devastating defeats at Stalingrad and Kursk to the relentless Soviet advance and the Allies’ storming of Normandy. You’ll discover how Hitler’s disastrous decisions, the overwhelming force of the Red Army, and the Allied bombing campaigns sealed Berlin’s fate. Explore the chaos within the German command, the fear among civilians, and the horrific street battles as the city was reduced to rubble. Learn about the tragedies of refugees, the vengeance of Soviet troops, and the grim final hours inside Hitler’s bunker.

The narrative delves into key events like the Warsaw Uprising, the bombing of Dresden, and the desperate defense by the Volkssturm and Hitler Youth. It also covers the emotional liberation of cities like Leningrad and Moscow, the horrors uncovered at concentration camps, and the political machinations between Stalin, Roosevelt, and Churchill that shaped postwar Europe. As Berlin fell, the video uncovers the immense suffering on both sides, the moral collapse of Nazi leadership, and the enduring human cost of total war.

If you’re interested in World War II history, the Eastern Front, or the dramatic end of Nazi Germany, this video provides a detailed, unflinching look at one of history’s darkest and most pivotal moments.

snippet.title: The Last Old-School Mafia Boss in Los Angeles
snippet.description:
The Last Don of Los Angeles: The Story of Nick "Old Man" Licata

While the Mafia in New York and Chicago chased headlines and high-profile hits, one man in Los Angeles ruled with a different code. His name was Nick Licata.

Known to the streets as "The Old Man," Licata was the last of the "Old World" Sicilian bosses. In today’s documentary, we trace his incredible journey from a marked man fleeing the Detroit Partnership to becoming the most respected figure in the Los Angeles crime family.

In this video, we explore:
-The Detroit Exile: Why the Zerilli-Tocco regime wanted Licata dead and how he escaped to California.
-The Five O’Clock Cafe: How a modest Burbank bar became the "White House" of the West Coast underworld.
-The Code of Omertà: The incredible story of Licata’s 1969 grand jury standoff where he chose a prison cell over a single word of testimony.
-The Mickey Mouse Mafia: The truth behind the L.A. family's reputation and why Licata was the only one who could keep it together.
-Nick Licata didn't believe in the flashy life of Hollywood mobsters. He believed in silence, tradition, and the long game. This is the story of the man who beat the FBI by never saying a word.

snippet.title: Sunken WWII Shipwrecks - The Hidden Oil Disaster Threatening Our Oceans
snippet.description:
Discover the hidden threat beneath our oceans - WWII shipwrecks leaking toxic oil, endangering coastlines and marine life. Are we running out of time to stop disaster?

This eye-opening documentary uncovers the alarming legacy of thousands of sunken World War II ships, many filled with millions of tons of oil that could trigger ecological catastrophes. Follow marine experts like Benedict Hack and international researchers as they investigate sites such as the Bay of Gdansk, where the wreck of the Stuttgart silently poisons the sea, and learn why governments worldwide are slow to act. From the Polish Riviera to Norway’s fjords and the US coast, see how oil leaks are already contaminating beaches, killing marine life, and threatening communities.

The video dives into the science of underwater oil pollution, the painstaking work of hydrographers, divers, and biologists, and the complex international legal battles over who is responsible for these ticking time bombs. You’ll hear firsthand accounts from NOAA researchers, salvage experts, and local fishermen whose livelihoods are at risk. With vivid footage of underwater wrecks and exclusive interviews, this exposé explores the costly solutions available - from sand sarcophagi to high-risk pumping operations - and the global inaction that could make future disasters inevitable. Will we wait until tragedy strikes, or take responsibility for this underwater legacy?

Kings and Generals animated historical documentary series on the Ancient Civilizations continues with an episode on how Rome conquered Greece. How did Rome conquer Greece, the birthplace of Alexander, the phalanx, and some of the most influential city-states in history? snippet.title: The Real Carlos Lehder Was the Most Dangerous Man in Blow
snippet.description:
December 7th, 1980. John Lennon is murdered outside the Dakota in New York City. 2,000 miles south, a 31 year old Colombian cocaine trafficker pops champagne and calls it a victory. His name was Carlos Lehder, and the Hollywood film Blow spent two hours making sure you’d never learn the truth about who he really was.

In this documentary, we tell the full untold story of Carlos Lehder Rivas, the half German, half Colombian narco who built the largest cocaine smuggling pipeline in human history alongside George Jung, then used the money to fund a fascist political party that openly worshipped Adolf Hitler.

What you’ll learn in this episode:
- How Lehder met George Jung in a Danbury, Connecticut federal prison in 1974 and drafted the entire Medellin Cartel smuggling model from a cell
- How he bought Norman’s Cay in the Bahamas in 1978 and terrorized its residents with armed guards, dobermans, rapes, and machine guns
- The 88,000 dollar monthly cash payment Lehder allegedly delivered to Bahamian Prime Minister Lynden Pindling every 22nd of the month
- The neo Nazi political party Lehder founded in Colombia called the Movimiento Latino Nacional, and his open praise of Adolf Hitler
- His 1987 extradition, the first major narco ever sent to the United States under the new treaty
- The 3.3 ton single shipment that helped earn him life plus 135 years
- His 1991 deal to testify against Panamanian dictator Manuel Noriega
- George Jung’s own 1994 cooperation deal, the part Blow refused to show you
- Lehder’s quiet 2020 release from federal prison and his current life in Bonn, Germany

Key figures: 
Carlos Lehder, George Jung, Pablo Escobar, Jorge Ochoa, Lynden Pindling, Manuel Noriega

Timeline: 
1949 birth, 1974 prison meeting, 1978 Norman’s Cay purchase, 1981 Nazi party founded, 1987 extradition, 1988 life sentence, 1991 Noriega testimony, 2020 release

This story matters because:
The cocaine smuggling blueprint Lehder invented in 1974 is still being used by every cartel operating in the Western Hemisphere today. And because Hollywood made a hero’s silhouette out of one of the most ideologically dangerous criminals of the 20th century.

Verified sources:
- United States v. Carlos Lehder Rivas, U S District Court for the Middle District of Florida, 1988 trial transcripts and verdict
- The Kings of Cocaine by Guy Gugliotta and Jeff Leen, Simon and Schuster, 1989
- DEA historical files on the Medellin Cartel and Norman’s Cay operations

snippet.description:
What really happened at Trafalgar… and why did Napoleon’s greatest ambition collapse in just a few hours? 🔔 Subscribe and join us on this journey around the world → https://bit.ly/WorldView-Documentary

Recreated using a new technique that allows characters to be superimposed onto a virtual background, here is the legendary Battle of Trafalgar. A spectacular first!
Since 1803, Napoleon had dreamed of invading England. For this ambition, the Emperor transformed the small port of Boulogne-sur-Mer into a gigantic fortress housing 150,000 soldiers. To ensure a successful landing, he sought to lure the British naval forces away from the English Channel. After several failed attempts to draw Collingwood's and Nelson's fleets to the West Indies, Admiral de Villeneuve allowed himself to be trapped off Cádiz, near Cape Trafalgar, hoping to draw the British there. But he soon received a counter-order and was forced to move to the Mediterranean. Two days after leaving the harbor, on October 21, 1805, the French ships commanded by Villeneuve were intercepted by twenty-seven English ships led by the flamboyant Admiral Nelson...A gripping military and human story with a face-off between two admirals who were complete opposites.
